title: Multi-class Semantic Segmentation of Photovoltaic Module Defects and Features: Towards Industrial Robotic Applications
mechanism: VGG16-UNet beat ResNet50 and MobileNet encoders on the 29-class SCDD; S: VGG gives the decoder a full-resolution 64-channel skip that the ResNet stem (stride 2 + maxpool) lacks, which matters for 1 to 2 px lines.
adaptation: U-Net++ with vgg16_bn encoder, or ResNet-34 plus a light full-res stem branch feeding the last decoder node; 1-ch input, house schedule; check gridline and crack, the two thin classes.
min_experiment: Arm full-res-skip U-Net++ vs house, 5 seeds; crack IoU, relF1@2, gridline IoU; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and gridline IoU < +0.03.
evidence: R: VGG16-UNet mean IoU 0.663 on features, 0.326 on defects, dead-cell IoU +0.129 vs prior; custom class weights. Chen 2023 (doi:10.1109/jphotov.2023.3249970) also used VGG16-UNet for crack, F1 0.875 IoU 0.782 on its own set.
prior_overlap: none: only ResNet-34/50 encoders tried; 2x input resolution (n.d.) is a different, 4x costlier change.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run their best (VGG16-UNet) under our fixed split and metrics as the label authors' reference baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run once, 3 seeds, under the benchmark protocol; report all-class and robust mIoU, crack relF1@2. No score kill line.

alt_notes.adaptation: Include it as the 'prior EL baseline' in the suite, re-run on our 24-class module-grouped splits and metrics to document why published numbers differ.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Run VGG16-UNet with class weights on our folds. Baseline: house. Expected to be below the house model; it is kept for comparability, not to raise scores.
